[F9] **External relative-cellular gluing input.** For the actual braid-axis filling $X=Y\cup_T(D^2\times S^1)$ with agreeing local coefficients, use finite CW representatives relative to the common boundary torus, with the based simple comparisons to the supplied exterior spines. The cellular inclusion and difference maps give the degreewise split exact gluing sequence. The based comparison is with those relative models, not with a core circle as a boundary-containing subcomplex. This is the geometric gluing/excision operation used in Conway, *Burau Maps and Twisted Alexander Polynomials*, arXiv:1510.06678v2, proof of Theorem 3.15, printed/PDF pp. 16–17; its based-chain multiplicativity is Proposition 2.4, printed/PDF p. 7. This finite relative-cellular comparison is an explicit external input, not a locally reconstructed relative-CW theorem. In the present proof the solid-torus comparison is additionally computed in step 2.3. The cellular operation applies after the declared color map as well: its degreewise splittings use individual lifted cells, so applying the coefficient representation preserves exactness; the only inverse needed in the solid-torus computation is the assumed invertible $M_n-I_d$. No acyclicity is assumed before that specialization. [Conway, Proposition 2.4 and proof of Theorem 3.15](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1510.06678v2)

replacements.after:
2.3 Give $D^2$ its boundary vertex, boundary edge $x$, and meridian disk cell $a$, and give $S^1$ its vertex and core edge $g_n$. Their product is a finite CW model $V_{\mathrm{rel}}$ of the actual solid torus containing exactly the specified torus CW structure as its boundary subcomplex. Besides the cells of $T$, it has the $2$-cell $a\times\{*\}$, still denoted $a$, and the $3$-cell $b=a\times g_n$. Put $A=M_n-I_d$ and let $q$ denote the torus $2$-cell, with the orientation in step 2.1. For a coefficient row $v$, the product boundaries are
$$\partial a(v)=x(v),\qquad \partial q(v)=x(-vA),\qquad \partial b(v)=q(v)+a(vA).$$
The first formula is the meridian disk boundary, the second is the torus Fox boundary from step 2.1, and the third is the oriented boundary of disk times core edge; its two terms have cancelling images under $\partial$. Replace the degree-two block $q(v)$ by $q'(v)=q(v)+a(vA)$. This block-triangular basis change has determinant one, $\partial q'=0$, and $\partial b(v)=q'(v)$. Split off the unit two-term pair $(b,q')$, then the unit pair $(a,x)$. The remaining based complex is exactly the core complex with $\partial g_n(v)=vA$. Each split pair has identity incidence and torsion one up to the sign unit, and the triangular change contributes determinant one. Hence $V_{\mathrm{rel}}$ has the same homology and torsion class as $V_{\mathrm{core}}$, so it is acyclic and its torsion is $D^{-1}$ up to the declared units. This calculation supplies the missing based comparison while retaining $T$ in the actual gluing model. [F1, F5, given, step 1.1, step 2.1, construct, algebra]

3.1 Use the relative-cellular gluing operation [F9] for the actual decomposition in the supplied certificate. For $V$ use $V_{\mathrm{rel}}$ from step 2.3, not its core spine. For the exterior pieces the operation uses the compatible relative CW representatives and the supplied based simple-spine comparisons. Equivalently, a boundary map into a spine is represented by its finite cellular mapping cylinder: each added prism over a torus cell pairs with its source face, with lifted incidence a unit; these pairs are removed in decreasing cell dimension. Their torsion changes lie in the declared unit subgroup. Thus the based torsion classes used below are those of the supplied spines, without identifying the boundary torus with a subcomplex of a core circle or of an abstract presentation. In the common relative models each cell of $T$ occurs in both pieces, and each other cell occurs in exactly one. Inclusion into the first piece and its negative into the second, followed by the difference quotient to the union, therefore give the degreewise split short exact sequence
$$0\longrightarrow C_*(T)\longrightarrow C_*(Y_{\mathrm{rel}})\oplus C_*(V_{\mathrm{rel}})\longrightarrow C_*(X_{\mathrm{rel}})\longrightarrow0.$$
Choose the shared lifts compatibly; any permitted adjustment changes only the declared determinant/deck units. Since $T$ and $V_{\mathrm{rel}}$ are acyclic by steps 2.1 and 2.3, the long exact homology sequence identifies $H_*(Y;Q^d)$ with $H_*(X;Q^d)$. Thus $Y$ is acyclic exactly when $X$ is. Subsequent references to the gluing sequence mean these relative models and their certified based comparisons. [F9, given, step 2.1, step 2.3, algebra]
